core_obligations: Write the closure of the extension as the intersection of its sums with a fundamental system of open ideals of the target (proof lines 1172-1176).

Compute the completed tensor product with the quotient as a limit of tensor products of quotients and rewrite it as a limit of quotients of the target by the sums of the extension with the open ideals of the source (proof lines 1176-1181).
Use continuity to see that each open ideal of one kind contains one of the other, simplify the limit, and conclude the identification with the closure (proof lines 1181-1184).
proof_roadmap: The closure as an intersection (proof lines 1172-1176).
The completed tensor product as a limit of quotients (proof lines 1176-1181).
difficulty_reason: For a continuous map of linearly topologized rings and an ideal of the source, the lemma identifies the closure of the extension of that ideal with the kernel of the canonical map from the target to the completed tensor product of the target with the quotient by the ideal (statement lines 1164-1170). The proof writes the closure as the intersection of the sums of the extension with a fundamental system of open ideals, computed by the description of closures as intersections, and then computes the completed tensor product as a limit of tensor products of quotients, which it rewrites as a limit of quotients of the target by the relevant ideals (proof lines 1172-1181). The final step uses continuity of the map to see that each member of one fundamental system is contained in a member of the other, so that the limit simplifies to the limit over the sums of the extension with the open ideals, which makes the identification immediate (proof lines 1181-1184). The claim is H2: the two descriptions are computed and then compared, and the comparison uses continuity in a stated way rather than being asserted.
